source.title: Backtracking Improves Generation Safety
source.authors: Yiming Zhang; Jianfeng Chi; Hailey Nguyen; K. Upasani; D. Bikel; Jason E. Weston; E. Smith

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether prefilling, adversarial prompt modifications, and decoding choices bypass safety, using attack success and harmful-response rates. It does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position KL methods.
record.gate_note: The paper cites harmful-data fine-tuning from prior work but does not test it. Its own backtracking training results and safety evaluations are recorded as findings that fit none of the listed versions. Rows focus on adversarial attack outcomes and decoding changes relevant to V4; Table 1 benchmark-specific rates are not separately extracted, while its overall rates are recorded.
record.test_reason: The baseline SFT/SFT+DPO models (base models safety-tuned on HH-RLHF) are attacked with prefilling, GCG suffixes, AutoDAN and temperature sampling, and ASR and unsafe rates are reported. This bears on V4. Backtracking trains the model to recover after an unsafe prefix, so it spreads safety beyond the opening. Its robustness under the same attacks bears on V7. The method differs from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that backtracking gives substantial safety gains over standard tuning without hurting helpfulness, and adds protection against all four attacks. They also note that all models stay far from adequate adversarial robustness, and that safety under sampling remains insufficient.
record.recipe_differences: Trains base models with a special [RESET] recovery mechanism, using SFT and DPO; the claim's original fine-tuning work uses harmful or benign examples to alter safety behaviour. This paper evaluates attack and decoding vulnerability rather than token-position KL or safety localization.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with training stage (SFT versus SFT + DPO), attack type, and decoding choice. Backtracking SFT has low reset rates and largely fails against optimization-based attacks; sampling and [RESET] logit bias change unsafe rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Backtracking SFT+DPO lowers overall greedy safety violations (Gemma 10.8% to 6.1%, Llama 5.2% to 1.5%) with similar MT-Bench scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery-token training reduces standard safety violations without a utility cost.

record.problems: Only two model families are tested. GCG and AutoDAN attack results use a random sample of 200 prompts; no uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported. Safety labels use Llama Guard 2. Some plotted logit-bias values are not numerically given in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's separate AdvBench, MaliciousInstructions, SimpleSafetyTests, and StrongReject rates are omitted; the overall rates are retained in r42-r49. Figure 3's intermediate logit-bias safety, latency, and throughput values are not extracted because only plotted values are supplied; the explicitly described -20 comparison is recorded in r41. Reset rates paired with attack success rates are noted in the corresponding rows rather than added as separate measures.

untested.parts: No harmful-data fine-tuning; Qi et al. is only cited.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No test of why alignment is shallow.
Robustness of backtracking to later fine-tuning attacks is not tested, and it is explicitly out of scope.

missing.what: Backtrack frequency on safety sets after SFT vs DPO (2.4%/0.2% vs 60.6%/49.9%), which explains why SFT-only recovery fails

record.verdict_notes: V7 is linked because backtracking trains recovery after an unsafe prefix, which deepens safety beyond the opening. The reader had marked V7 not tested. Baseline models are the authors' own safety-tuned base models, not production chat models. ASR comes from Llama Guard 2; GCG and AutoDAN use 200 prompts, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune safety-trained chat models on harmful examples or report resulting harmful compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data for its effect on harmful compliance.
Does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence or its distribution across response positions.
Tests prefilling, optimization-based prompt attacks, sampling, and a [RESET] logit-bias change. It does not test whether arbitrary compliant openings or all decoding changes bypass safety.
Does not localize safety behaviour to weights, parameters, or ranks.
Does not test why safety is shallow or whether the training data/objective produces shallowness.
Backtracking is a recovery method, not a test of spreading safety beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Tables 2 and 8 show incomplete Gemma prefill bypasses at 50.4% and 53.3%, weaker than Llama's 85.0% and 85.6%.

relationships.condition: Backtracking SFT+DPO against prefilling and single-sample decoding
relationships.reason: Recovery training cuts prefill ASR from 50.4% to 11.6% and from 85% to 2.6%, and keeps sampled unsafe rates near greedy. Suppressing reset doubles unsafety (r2,r10,r34,r36,r41).
relationships.display_finding: Backtracking training cut prefill attack success from 50.4% to 11.6% and from 85% to 2.6%, and sampled unsafe rates stayed near greedy levels. Suppressing the reset doubled unsafe outputs.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Backtracking SFT+DPO against prefilling and single-sample decoding
source_check.reason: Prefill ASR falls to 11.6% and 2.6%; single-sample unsafe rates remain near greedy rates. Suppressing RESET doubles Llama unsafety, supporting recovery's contribution.

relationships.condition: Backtracking SFT+DPO vs optimization attacks and worst-of-10; backtracking SFT vs prefilling
relationships.reason: ASR falls but stays 16.5–60% under GCG, AutoDAN and adaptive attacks, and worst-of-10 reaches 16–39%. SFT-only prefill ASR stays 22.7–25.2% (r4-r16,r18,r26,r38,r40).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success fell but stayed at 16.5–60% under GCG, AutoDAN and adaptive attacks, worst-of-10 sampling reached 16–39%, and SFT-only backtracking left prefill success at 22.7–25.2%.

source_check.condition: Backtracking SFT+DPO vs optimization attacks and worst-of-10; backtracking SFT vs prefilling
